status_legend.supported: independent check against current primary source agrees
status_legend.partly: source agrees on core; correction noted (README uses corrected form)
status_legend.not_rechecked: sourced with verbatim quote by a research angle, not in the independent verification pass
status_legend.unconfirmed: no primary source confirms it; listed in README section 7

note: Quotes are verbatim excerpts (shortened). Internal paths are relative to the repo root (or the user memory folder). No account IDs.

claims.claim: Under Billing Transfer the reseller's management account pays our org's whole consolidated bill (members included); we stay owner of our org.
claims.quote: A billing transfer is an arrangement between two management accounts where one management account manages and pays for the consolidated bill of the other management account, and member accounts under it.
claims.note: Only usage from the start date (1st of a month, 00:00 UTC); earlier usage stays with us.

claims.claim: We keep full administrative control (IAM, access, security, SCPs, account lifecycle); reseller takes over billing.
claims.quote: Billing transfer only affects billing relationships. You maintain full control over account access and permissions, resource management, security configurations, and all administrative functions.
claims.note: SCPs/account lifecycle implied, not named. Reseller also controls which prices/cost data we see via Billing Conductor.

claims.claim: An org can have only one outbound billing transfer; not adjustable. A different payer for the AI account needs another org or standalone.
claims.quote: This quota is not adjustable.
claims.note: 'At any given time': switching resellers is possible by withdraw + new invite.

claims.claim: Setup: reseller sends invitation (InviteOrganizationToTransferResponsibility, BILLING); we accept (ListHandshakesForAccount TRANSFER_RESPONSIBILITY, AcceptHandshake); both orgs all-features.
claims.quote: To respond to an invitation, you must have the following permissions actions: organizations:ListHandshakesAccount organizations:AcceptHandshake organizations:DeclineHandshake
claims.note: AWS page typo: real action is ListHandshakesForAccount. All-features requirement is on the best-practices page. Sender needs Billing Conductor permissions.

claims.claim: Only management accounts send invitations, and only the paying side.
claims.quote: Only the account that will manage and pay for the consolidated bill (bill-transfer account) can send invitations.
claims.note: Console setup requires Billing Conductor; API setup possible without.

claims.claim: Transfer starts 1st of a month (next month up to 6 months); accept >=24h before. Earliest from 31/10/2026 is 01/12/2026; November billed to us.
claims.quote: It can be the first day of any month from the next month up to six months in the future.
claims.note: AWS wording on cutoff is inconsistent; safe deadline 29/11/2026 23:59:59 UTC at the latest.

claims.claim: Marketplace purchases (Claude, proprietary OpenAI) still possible; invoices go to reseller, reseller's tax profile, notifications to reseller.
claims.quote: Your channel partner becomes responsible for paying for all your marketplace purchases.
claims.note: FAQ does not mention Bedrock; gpt-oss is not Marketplace. Partners 'may' use SCPs to keep PO off invoice.

claims.claim: Third-party models set up per account: auto-subscribe on first call needs aws-marketplace perms, Anthropic FTU (inheritable), valid Marketplace payment method; separate account-level gate may remain.
claims.quote: Access is determined separately for each AWS account, so accounts in the same AWS Organization can have different access.
claims.note: Only models with a Marketplace product ID auto-subscribe. Perms needed only for first call. AWS names AWS Sales (not Support) for the extra gate. FTU not needed on bedrock-mantle; can stay PENDING.

claims.claim: Anthropic FTU submitted once from our management account is inherited by members (opt-in regions excepted); under Billing Transfer that management account is ours.
claims.quote: The form submission at the root account will be inherited by other accounts in the same AWS Organization.
claims.note: Covers only the use-case step; Marketplace subscription and account-level access still per account.

claims.claim: Seller of record by provider: Anthropic sells Claude, OpenAI sells proprietary models; AWS sells gpt-oss, Meta, Mistral, DeepSeek, Qwen.
claims.quote: Anthropic Services on Amazon Bedrock are sold by Anthropic.
claims.note: Cohere, Stability, Luma, TwelveLabs, Writer (except Palmyra Vision 7B) also sell their own models with product IDs.

claims.claim: Providers not sold via Marketplace: Amazon, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, MiniMax, Mistral, Moonshot, NVIDIA, Qwen, xAI, Z.AI, plus OpenAI gpt-oss.
claims.quote: Models from the following providers aren't sold through AWS Marketplace and don't have product keys
claims.note: Confirmed by verification of B-B5/C-C5.

claims.claim: SPP Authorized Services List: reseller must hold Anthropic resale authority before it or its end customer uses Claude; whether Billing Transfer counts is the open point.
claims.quote: Before you or your End Customer can access and use any model offered by Anthropic, you must first apply for and obtain resale authority from Anthropic
claims.note: AWS What's New 2025-11-19: SPP/Distribution partners 'can now resell AWS services using Billing Transfer' -> gate logically applies; no page names Anthropic+Billing Transfer together (inference).

claims.claim: AWS announced Bedrock partner resale; Anthropic resale has limits.
claims.quote: *Resale of Anthropic models subject to certain limitations.
claims.note: See B-B9/C-C13.

claims.claim: Reseller sees our consumption and billing metadata (tags, cost categories) in Cost Explorer and CUR; prices what we see via Billing Conductor.
claims.quote: The bill transfer account can view the consumption and billing metadata (such as cost categories and cost allocation tags) of bill source accounts in Cost Explorer and AWS Cost and Usage Report.
claims.note: Not in the independent verification pass; consistent with D-D8/D-D9 checks.

claims.claim: We lose visibility: pro forma only, existing CUR Unhealthy, Cost Anomaly Detection stops alerting, no hourly granularity.
claims.quote: CAD is not supported for bill-source accounts. As a bill-source account, existing monitors and newly created monitors won't generate alerts.
claims.note: Confirmed in D-D9 verification.

claims.claim: Our credits still apply but to the bill AWS sends the reseller; Credits page no longer shows balance.
claims.quote: Your Credits page no longer displays your credit balance.
claims.note: Not re-checked; contract must pass savings through.

claims.claim: Activate credits can offset Marketplace fees for third-party Bedrock models; whether Lift credit does is unconfirmed.
claims.quote: may be applied to offset fees and charges for AWS Marketplace incurred for the use of third-party foundation models available on Amazon Bedrock
claims.note: Lift credit coverage unconfirmed (README U7).

claims.claim: Savings Plans, RIs and volume tiers stay calculated per org, not pooled with reseller's customers.
claims.quote: Volume discount tiers, Reserved Instances, and Savings Plans continue to be calculated and applied at the individual AWS Organizations level.
claims.note: Also stated in A-B2 verification note.

claims.claim: Billing Conductor: AWS managed plan free; customer managed plan 50 USD per org per month from 01/06/2026; who pays unclear.
claims.quote: there is a monthly fee of $50 per AWS Organization
claims.note: S261 spot-check: charged 'by the number of AWS Organizations that have a customer managed pricing plan attached'; payer between reseller and us still UNCONFIRMED (U8).

claims.claim: Either side can withdraw any time; ends 23:59:59 UTC last day of chosen month; irreversible; no account moves.
claims.quote: Either account involved in a transfer can withdraw the transfer at any time.
claims.note: End month can only be current or next month. A payment method on our side before the end date is our inference, not documented.

claims.claim: As a member of reseller's org, reseller can attach SCPs, remove accounts, block leaving; leaving loses org agreements and Cost Explorer history; OrganizationAccountAccessRole stays.
claims.quote: Note that the organization administrator can apply a policy to your account that removes this permission, preventing you from removing your account from the organization.
claims.note: OrganizationAccountAccessRole is auto-created only for accounts created in the org. acc2/acc3 org membership is from internal records, not AWS docs.

claims.claim: Management account is the payer and has final control; SCPs never restrict it.
claims.quote: The management account is the ultimate owner of the organization, having final control over security, infrastructure, and finance policies.
claims.note: Standard Organizations behaviour.

claims.claim: Since Nov 2025 an account can move directly between orgs without standing alone.
claims.quote: eliminates the previous requirement for the account to temporarily operate as a standalone account
claims.note: S261 spot-check: 'an organization invites an account, and the account accepts the invite'; available in all commercial regions.

claims.claim: Since 15/10/2025 serverless models are open by default in commercial regions; control via IAM and SCP.
claims.quote: Amazon Bedrock now provides immediate access to all serverless foundation models by default
claims.note: Correction: PutFoundationModelEntitlement is still listed as an IAM action; the Model access page now applies only to GovCloud. Marketplace subscription, FTU, payment method and account-level access still apply.

claims.claim: Anthropic FTU via PutUseCaseForModelAccess, once per account or once at management account; members inherit; not for opt-in regions; not needed on bedrock-mantle.
claims.quote: Anthropic requires first-time customers to submit use case details before invoking a model once per account or once at the organization's management account.
claims.note: Check status via agreementAvailability.status (not authorizationStatus). Form fields: companyName, companyWebsite, intendedUsers, industryOption, otherIndustryOption, useCases.

claims.claim: Org-level FTU inheritance only works when submitted via API from management account (Security blog).
claims.quote: Its approval automatically extends to the child accounts within your organization (but only if done via the API).
claims.note: The current User Guide does not repeat the API-only condition; submitting via API satisfies both.

claims.claim: Marketplace-sold models auto-subscribe per account on first call; first caller needs Subscribe/Unsubscribe/ViewSubscriptions; account needs valid payment method; up to 15 minutes.
claims.quote: When you invoke a third-party model for the first time in your account, Amazon Bedrock automatically initiates the subscription process in the background.
claims.note: After enablement, other principals need no Marketplace perms.

claims.claim: Which providers go through Marketplace (product IDs: Claude Sonnet 5.5 prod-pjfguoisodbd6, GPT-5.5 prod-indw4nwkcsyua).
claims.quote: These models are available to all Amazon Bedrock users and don't require a AWS Marketplace subscription.
claims.note: Command R+ reached end of life 2026-08-19 (bad example; use Cohere Embed v4). Other providers (AI21, Writer X4/X5, Luma, Stability, TwelveLabs) must be checked per model card.

claims.claim: Marketplace-sold models are billed under the model provider, not Amazon Bedrock.
claims.quote: Charges appear on your AWS bill and in AWS Cost Explorer under the model provider (not under Amazon Bedrock).
claims.note: Same sentence on Cohere Embed v4 card (prod-ft3cj5gst3spo). GPT cards have product IDs but not the sentence. 'Payer matters' is our inference.

claims.claim: Even with FTU, subscription and payment, an account can be refused: additional account-level access, per account; contact AWS Sales. Error 002 text not in AWS docs.
claims.quote: Some models require additional account-level access.
claims.note: AWS does not name which models. Community reports Error 002 as ValidationException vs docs' AccessDeniedException; link to acc3 is inference. Rule out PENDING agreement first.

claims.claim: Under Billing Transfer Marketplace invoices (incl. Bedrock third-party) go to the reseller; partners may use SCPs for PO handling.
claims.quote: Channel partners may choose to prevent your PO from appearing on their invoice by implementing Service Control Policies (SCPs).
claims.note: Ask reseller whether bill-transfer setup counts as valid Marketplace payment method (U4).

claims.claim: Partner resale of Anthropic has limitations documented in Partner Central; Vietnam is on Anthropic's supported countries.
claims.quote: *Resale of Anthropic models subject to certain limitations.
claims.note: Not 'only' Partner Central: 2026 partner announcements say Anthropic runs its own reseller approval. Written VN+Billing Transfer confirmation is our recommendation, not an AWS rule.

claims.claim: Converse authorizes as InvokeModel; ConverseStream as InvokeModelWithResponseStream; no provider condition key.
claims.quote: ConverseStream bedrock-runtime ... bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream
claims.note: Consistent with Security blog note that denying InvokeModel also blocks Converse.

claims.claim: us.* profile needs InvokeModel on profile ARN, source FM and every destination FM; from us-west-1 Sonnet 5.5 routes to us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1, us-west-2; InferenceProfileArn exception cannot bypass source region.
claims.quote: If your organization's security policy uses SCPs to block unused Regions, you must either allow access to all destination Regions listed in the Geographic cross-Region inference profile for your source Region or add an inference-profile exception
claims.note: Destinations vary by source region and model; confirm with GetInferenceProfile. Sonnet 5.5 has no in-region support in us-west-1.

claims.claim: global.* needs region-less FM ARN; aws:RequestedRegion = unspecified; ~10% cheaper than geographic.
claims.quote: For this evaluation, the service sets aws:RequestedRegion to unspecified rather than the actual destination AWS Region.
claims.note: Source region must still be allowed by the SCP.

claims.claim: Denying aws-marketplace:Subscribe does not block first call; deny bedrock:InvokeModel* or bedrock:* on model ARNs; deleting agreement does not block.
claims.quote: Denying aws-marketplace:Subscribe alone will not block the first model invocation, because Amazon Bedrock auto-initiates the subscription in the background.
claims.note: DenyDeepseekEverywhere sample is from the Security blog. Test deny on bedrock-mantle separately.

claims.claim: Marketplace perms can be scoped with aws:CalledViaLast = bedrock.amazonaws.com and aws-marketplace:ProductId.
claims.quote: "aws:CalledViaLast": "bedrock.amazonaws.com"
claims.note: Used as optional statement in README IAM example.

claims.claim: Managed entitlements: management account subscribes once and grants members via License Manager; licenses in us-east-1; private offer price applies only to accepting account until grants.
claims.quote: Managed entitlements for Amazon Bedrock solves this by letting you subscribe once from a management account and distribute access to member accounts across your AWS Organization.
claims.note: S261 spot-check: 'All licenses are created in the us-east-1 region'; 'request that private offers ... be issued to your management account'.

claims.claim: OpenAI GPT-5.5 on bedrock-runtime in us-west-1 only via us./global. profiles; needs InvokeModel on project/default; mantle action bedrock-mantle:CreateInference, GPT-5.5 mantle only us-east-1/2.
claims.quote: Your IAM identity also needs bedrock:InvokeModel on your account's default project (arn:aws:bedrock:{region}:{account-id}:project/default)
claims.note: Same pattern confirmed on GPT-5.6 Terra card (C-C18).

claims.claim: Billing Transfer leaves our governance intact; consolidated bill priced to us through Billing Conductor.
claims.quote: Separate billing and administration: The management account that accepted the invitation maintains complete administration over its organization
claims.note: Same evidence as A-B1/A-B2.

claims.claim: Account-level gate separate from self-service steps; per account; AWS Sales route. Closest official description of Error 002.
claims.quote: If you complete the activation requirements and verify that the model is supported in the AWS Region but still receive an `AccessDeniedException`, contact AWS Sales for additional access options.
claims.note: 'Closest description' is inference; page says 'some models'. Rule out IAM/SCP conditions, Marketplace perms, payment method, PENDING agreement first.

claims.claim: A quota increase does not grant account-level access.
claims.quote: A quota increase doesn't grant additional account-level access to a model.
claims.note: Ask 'grant this account access' only after ruling out ordinary causes.

claims.claim: Three per-account prerequisites for Marketplace-sold models; up to 2 min after fix, up to 15 min setup.
claims.quote: After granting the necessary permissions, it may take up to 2 minutes for the subscription to complete
claims.note: Model access page retired only in commercial regions. Perms needed only for first caller. FTU inheritable; PENDING wait separate.

claims.claim: Marketplace perms only for first enabling call; afterwards invoker needs only bedrock:InvokeModel; enabling call must satisfy InvokeModel conditions.
claims.quote: These permissions are only required the first time a model is being used in an account.
claims.note: aws:SourceIp conditions cannot be met via VPC endpoint. Streaming and cross-region need extra actions/resources.

claims.claim: Non-Marketplace providers skip Marketplace perms and payment checks; if Nova/Mistral also refused, cause is the account.
claims.quote: Some providers sell only part of their model catalog through AWS Marketplace.
claims.note: Last step overstated: also IAM/SCP denies, region availability, project/default before concluding account-level gate. GPT-5.4 product ID prod-3bbohv3635iau.

claims.claim: FTU once per account or at management account; PENDING until AVAILABLE; API inheritance per blog.
claims.quote: The model agreement can enter a pending state, during which invoking the model continues to return AccessDeniedException even though your submission succeeded.
claims.note: Current guide console text does not repeat API-only condition.

claims.claim: FTU inheritance only via API (Security blog).
claims.quote: (but only if done via the API)
claims.note: See B-B3.

claims.claim: Marketplace agreement failure (403): common causes invalid payment and restricted geo-location; no official fix procedure.
claims.quote: Common underlying issues are invalid payment error and restricted geo-location.
claims.note: 'Common', not 'most often'. Reseller-payer payment instrument link is our inference.

claims.claim: Default quotas can be lower for an account based on age, usage and payment history; increases not automatic.
claims.quote: As a result, the quotas that apply to your account might be lower than the default values listed
claims.note: Check per account, per region, per endpoint; embeddings limited by RPM.

claims.claim: Raise runtime quotas via 'Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for <model>'; priority to accounts using quota; no increases for Legacy/Deprecated.
claims.quote: Due to overwhelming demand, priority will be given to customers who generate traffic that consumes their existing quota allocation.
claims.note: Correction: General Reference does publish L-codes (Sonnet 4.6 cross-region TPM L-15B8E632, Haiku 4.5 L-58BE175A). RPM not in the bundle.

claims.claim: bedrock-mantle quotas separate; increases via AWS Support limit form, not Service Quotas console.
claims.quote: quota increase requests are not currently processed through the Service Quotas console.
claims.note: Used in README step 9.

claims.claim: Anthropic and OpenAI sell their models; Meta and Mistral sold by AWS; Anthropic bans unapproved resale; OpenAI limited to Supported Countries.
claims.quote: resell the Services except as expressly approved by Anthropic.
claims.note: 'Payer matters for Claude/GPT' is our inference, not an AWS rule.

claims.claim: SPP/Distribution partners may resell Bedrock since 14/10/2025; Anthropic limited; terms not public.
claims.quote: Resale of Anthropic models subject to certain limitations.
claims.note: Provider list also includes AI21, Luma, Stability, TwelveLabs. 2026 partner releases: separate Anthropic approval required.

claims.claim: Under Billing Transfer Marketplace purchases invoiced to reseller; we keep admin control; coordinate with partner.
claims.quote: When you purchase products from AWS Marketplace, your invoices are transferred to your channel partner's Bill-Transfer account.
claims.note: No AWS doc says reseller must 'explicitly accept' Marketplace charges; that is a contract question.

claims.claim: Billing questions to channel partner first; AWS Support handles billing transfer / Marketplace integration problems.
claims.quote: For platform issues, AWS Support can help resolve billing transfer and AWS Marketplace integration problems
claims.note: Used in README section 6.

claims.claim: With Resold Support, AWS Support does not handle billing/account issues; Basic plan can open account/billing and limit-increase cases, not technical.
claims.quote: AWS Support can't assist with non-technical issues for Resold Support, such as billing and account management.
claims.note: Only 'Resold Support' is named; Partner-Led Support restriction not stated. Which case type covers Error 002 is inference.

claims.claim: Billing Transfer mechanics: accept 24h before start; CAD not supported; credits not visible.
claims.quote: Invites must be accepted 24 hours before the start date of the billing transfer, in UTC time.
claims.note: Consistent with A-B6/A-B15 verification.

claims.claim: In us-west-1 Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-5.6 Terra only via us./global. profiles; GPT-5.6 needs project/default; mantle in us-east-1/2, us-west-2.
claims.quote: This model is not available for in-Region inference on that endpoint.
claims.note: Used in README provider table.

claims.claim: Claude on Bedrock billed through Marketplace under the provider; credit coverage not stated on card.
claims.quote: This model is a third-party model offered and billed through AWS Marketplace.
claims.note: Credit coverage UNCONFIRMED (U7).

claims.claim: Vietnam is on Anthropic's supported countries list.
claims.quote: Vietnam
claims.note: Covers 'Claude models offered through cloud platforms and authorized resellers' (per B-B9 verification). Geo-check attribute unconfirmed (U13).

claims.claim: Private offer accepted by management account can be distributed; otherwise members pay public rates until grants.
claims.quote: If you accept this offer from any other account, you cannot distribute it from AWS Marketplace, and member accounts continue to be billed at public rates until you create grants in AWS License Manager.
claims.note: Consistent with S261 spot-check of managed-entitlements page.

claims.claim: 'Error 002' appears only in community re:Post threads (incl. org members vended same day), fixed via Support case.
claims.quote: bedrock error 002 access to bedrock models is not allowed for this account on four organization member accounts vended the same day
claims.note: Thread body returned 403; title only. Low confidence.

claims.claim: Access decided per account, so fewer Bedrock-calling accounts means fewer accounts that can be refused.
claims.quote: Access is determined separately for each AWS account, so accounts in the same AWS Organization can have different access.
claims.note: Overstated: FTU and org SCPs are org-wide; per-account parts are Marketplace agreement, payment method, extra access. Valid but moderate argument.

claims.claim: AWS SRA for AI separates Application and Generative AI accounts but allows merging; single gen-AI account for pre-trained models.
claims.quote: Merge the Application and Generative AI accounts if your architecture requires consolidating both services in one account, or if your generative AI usage spans your entire organization.
claims.note: The 'single account' bullet is about one vs several gen-AI accounts, not merging app+AI.

claims.claim: SRA benefits: OU/account-specific SCPs, simpler least privilege; option to split gen-AI accounts by SDLC.
claims.quote: This account separation provides two key benefits.
claims.note: SDLC split is one option, not a recommendation; guide assumes a single gen-AI account with IAM roles.

claims.claim: TPM quotas per model per region per account; daily token cap per account per region; shared AI account means dev waves compete with prod.
claims.quote: Maximum tokens per day across all supported Amazon Bedrock models for this account.
claims.note: Separate account only helps if prod uses its own credentials.

claims.claim: New accounts may start below defaults; keep account with history or warm up early.
claims.quote: the default quotas assigned to an account might be updated depending on regional factors, account age, usage history, payment history
claims.note: Recommendation is inference; quotas per region and per endpoint.

claims.claim: Application inference profiles give per-app cost on InvokeModel/Converse; not supported by Responses/Chat Completions (400).
claims.quote: Application inference profiles aren't supported by the Responses and Chat Completions APIs, on either endpoint.
claims.note: Tags must be activated; up to 24h; not retroactive.

claims.claim: IAM principal attribution records calling role per request on runtime and mantle; session tags need sts:TagSession; cache credentials.
claims.quote: Amazon Bedrock automatically captures the IAM principal identity (IAM users and IAM roles) for every inference request.
claims.note: Needs tag activation in payer account, new CUR 2.0 export with caller identity; daily granularity; AWS positions it for user-level attribution.

claims.claim: Cost allocation tags activated only from management/payer account; under Billing Transfer bill-source manages its tags.
claims.quote: Member accounts don't have access to the cost allocation tags manager
claims.note: Tag filtering on bill-source pro forma Cost Explorer UNCONFIRMED (U9).

claims.claim: Bill-source loses CAD, CUR becomes inactive, pro forma only; separate AI account gives clean cost line.
claims.quote: After transfer, existing AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) configurations become inactive and display as Unhealthy.
claims.note: CUR can be reconfigured. Bedrock/Marketplace already appear as separate service lines, so cost alone does not justify a separate account.

claims.claim: Anthropic FTU at management account covers every member; extra accounts add no Anthropic paperwork.
claims.quote: once per account or once at the organization's management account

claims.quote: Amazon Bedrock supports resource-based policies for guardrails and guardrail inference profiles.
claims.note: Supports keeping the satellite assume-role pattern.

claims.quote: automatically enforces configured safeguards across all member entities

claims.quote: Allow "aws:RequestedRegion": "unspecified"
